solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Occasion to eat small part of shoe (6)

blocks.note: S = small, as on clothing labels
the upper is the part of a shoe above the sole

annotation.surface: A cobbler describing a small component of a shoe.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all footwear; 'Occasion to eat' has to be peeled off the front as a meal.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the last meal of the day is literally an occasion for eating.

entries.clue: Use dismissive words, specifically inappropriate (5)

blocks.note: a remark that is off is out of order

annotation.surface: A complaint about someone's rude, out-of-place remarks.
annotation.walkthrough: SC is the scholarly abbreviation for scilicet, used in footnotes to mean 'that is to say'.
annotation.definitionFit: To scoff is to speak with scorn and derision.

entries.clue: Shoot British tanker as mercenary work? (9)

blocks.note: pot = shoot, as in pot a rabbit
an oiler is an oil tanker

annotation.surface: A soldier of fortune hired to fire on a British oil tanker.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mercenary work' suggests hired guns, which the surface sets up; here it is writing done just to earn money.
annotation.definitionFit: A potboiler is a book written only to pay the bills, work done for money.

entries.clue: Prophet latterly seen in the Ritz or Astoria (4)

indicatorNotes.latterly: take the latter, final, letter of each word

annotation.surface: A holy man glimpsed at a smart London hotel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Latterly' reads as 'recently'; here it takes the last letter of the words that follow.
annotation.definitionFit: Ezra is a prophet and scribe of the Old Testament.

entries.clue: Build audible pop that frightens me (8)

indicatorNotes.audible: what is heard, not what is written, gives the answer

blocks.note: pop is fizzy drink, or fizz
'eek!' is what you cry when something frightens you

annotation.surface: Someone startled by the sound of a bottle popping open.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Build' looks like a verb opening an instruction, and it is the noun: a person's build. FIZZ-EEK said quickly is PHYSIQUE.
annotation.definitionFit: Your physique is your build, the shape of your body.

entries.clue: Trendy joint forbidding closing early (7)

indicatorNotes.closing early: the word ends early, losing its last letter

annotation.surface: A fashionable bar with a stern policy of shutting early.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Joint' and 'closing early' conjure a nightclub; the joint is a body part and 'forbidding' is an adjective, not a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, noun for noun: 'a trendy' is British slang for someone who chases fashion.

entries.clue: Soldier in RUC somehow stops raid with military precision (10)

indicatorNotes.in: the soldier is in, inside, the rearranged RUC
indicatorNotes.somehow: done somehow, in some unspecified way, so RUC's letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.stops: a stopper plugs a gap, so the result plugs the middle of the raid

blocks.note: a sally is a sudden attack out of a besieged place

annotation.surface: Security forces in Northern Ireland carrying out a precise raid.
annotation.walkthrough: S(UR(GI)C)ALLY. The RUC was the Royal Ulster Constabulary, Northern Ireland's police force until 2001.
annotation.definitionFit: A surgical strike is precise, so acting surgically is acting with military precision.

entries.clue: Still using linen primarily for fourth duvet (5)

indicatorNotes.using: QUIET puts the new letter to use, taking it on board
indicatorNotes.primarily: primarily means first of all, so take the first letter of linen
indicatorNotes.for fourth: L goes in place of, instead of, the fourth letter

blocks.note: QUIET (still), minus its fourth letter E
the first letter of Linen, put in fourth place

annotation.surface: Bedding advice: keep things calm by using linen for a duvet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Still' is the adjective quiet, not the adverb 'yet'. QUIET with L in place of its fourth letter becomes QUILT.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a duvet is a thick, stuffed bed cover, which is a continental quilt.

entries.clue: Seeing all of each delight — once you would (5-4)

annotation.surface: An old-fashioned wish that you might enjoy every pleasure.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks archaic language: ye was the old plural 'you'.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone eagle-eyed misses nothing, seeing all.

entries.clue: Steadying frame needed for dais/plinth (6)

indicatorNotes.needed for: the answer is found within the letters that follow

annotation.surface: A builder's note that a supporting frame is required for the platform.
annotation.walkthrough: The slash between dais and plinth is ignored, letting the answer straddle it.
annotation.definitionFit: A splint is a rigid support that holds a broken bone steady.

entries.clue: Produce better harvest than bare rock (7)

blocks.note: read as OUT (beat) + CROP (produce a harvest), like outrun or outplay
geology: bedrock exposed where the soil is missing

annotation.surface: Farming talk: out-yielding a field that is nothing but bare rock.
annotation.walkthrough: The first sense is an invented but fair verb built like outrun or outplay; the second is the ordinary geological noun.
annotation.definitionFit: An outcrop is a patch of bedrock exposed at the surface.

entries.clue: Sixth wife finally turned to different monarch for deposition (7)

indicatorNotes.finally: points at the last letter of PARR
indicatorNotes.turned to: the letter changes into something else

blocks.note: Catherine PARR was Henry VIII's sixth wife; her final R is replaced
R (Rex, a monarch) becomes a different monarch, KING

annotation.surface: A Tudor history note about a queen being replaced and a king deposed.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface steers 'deposition' towards removing a monarch; here it is simply putting something down, as you deposit a car in a space.
annotation.definitionFit: Parking is the depositing of a vehicle somewhere.

entries.clue: Loud noise of bull run (4)

annotation.surface: A bull charging and bellowing loudly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bull run' pairs up as a stampede; the definition is just the last word, run as water runs.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the verb sense of liquid moving: rivers and taps both run.

entries.clue: Composer Olive abandons orphan in rancour (10)

indicatorNotes.abandons: to abandon is to walk away, so OLIVE departs from the orphan's full name
indicatorNotes.in: what is left of the name sits in, inside, the word for rancour

blocks.note: Dickens's orphan OLIVER TWIST without OLIVE

annotation.surface: A woman named Olive coldly walking out on an orphan.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Olive' looks like a person, but it is letters to strip from Oliver Twist. BI(RTWIST)LE: Sir Harrison Birtwistle was an English modernist composer.
annotation.definitionFit: Harrison Birtwistle was a leading English composer.

entries.clue: Both of us doing big walks in Yorkshire area (4,6)

annotation.surface: A couple hiking energetically in the Yorkshire Dales.
annotation.walkthrough: The West Riding was one of the three historic divisions of Yorkshire, in northern England.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: one of three historic ridings, the old administrative thirds of the county, around Leeds and Bradford.

entries.clue: Unnatural material, caustic stuff included by blogger? (9)

indicatorNotes.included by: something included by another thing is contained in it, so LYE goes inside POSTER

blocks.note: a blogger is someone who posts; the question mark flags the example

annotation.surface: A blogger ranting about synthetic fabric and harsh chemicals.
annotation.walkthrough: PO(LYE)STER. The question mark admits that a blogger is only one kind of poster.
annotation.definitionFit: Polyester is a synthetic fibre, not a natural one.

entries.clue: One Topic has nuts, but not this one (9)

annotation.definition: One Topic has nuts, but not this one

indicatorNotes.nuts: crazy, so the letters are jumbled

annotation.surface: A remark that the Topic chocolate bar contains nuts, just not this kind.
annotation.walkthrough: Topic is a British chocolate bar with hazelnuts. 'Nuts' is both the anagram signal and, in the whole clue, what the answer is: a nut absent from Topic.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue is true: the Topic bar uses hazelnuts, so this green nut is one it lacks.

entries.clue: Positive vote returned with more than one bishop in religious building (5)

indicatorNotes.returned: something returned goes back the way it came, so YEA is written backwards
indicatorNotes.in: the bishops are placed in, inside, the reversed vote

blocks.note: B = bishop in chess notation, doubled

annotation.surface: Church business: a vote passed with several bishops present.
annotation.walkthrough: YEA is the parliamentary word for a yes vote. Bishops and a religious building sit so naturally together that the building reads as scene-setting, not the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a monastery's church, like Westminster Abbey, is one kind of religious building.

entries.clue: Fighters lay stick across ankle bones (9)

indicatorNotes.across: the stick lies across, around, the bones

blocks.note: tali, plural of talus, the ankle bone

annotation.surface: Soldiers setting a splint across an injured ankle.
annotation.walkthrough: BAT(TALI)ON. TALI is the Latin plural of talus, the ankle bone.
annotation.definitionFit: A battalion is a body of fighting troops.

entries.clue: No big fish failed to move, holding pair (5)

indicatorNotes.holding: SAT holds PR the way hands hold something, around it

annotation.surface: Someone who is nobody important froze, clutching a couple of things.
annotation.walkthrough: S(PR)AT. 'No big fish' reads as 'nobody important', and it is literally a small fish.
annotation.definitionFit: Literal reading of an idiom: 'no big fish' usually means a nobody, and a tiny herring-like fish fits it word for word.

entries.clue: Worked until due day at full strength (9)

indicatorNotes.Worked: the letters are worked into a new order

annotation.surface: An employee working flat out right up to the deadline.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Worked' passes as the verb of a work diary; it is telling you to rearrange UNTIL DUE plus D.
annotation.definitionFit: Undiluted means not watered down, at full strength.

entries.clue: Condition that is to fill cracked urn? I’ll make us one (7)

indicatorNotes.to fill: filling goes into a container, so IF and IE go inside
indicatorNotes.cracked: a cracked pot is broken, so URN's letters are broken up and rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone offering to mend a cracked urn and unite the pieces.
annotation.walkthrough: UN(IF IE)R. The definition is spoken by the answer itself: a unifier is someone who says 'I'll make us one'.
annotation.definitionFit: A unifier joins things together, making them one.
annotation.definitionNote: the definition is a sentence the unifier would say

entries.clue: Whoever does the work coats for doctor upped game (6)

indicatorNotes.coats for: take the coat, the outside letters, of each word

annotation.surface: A doctor raising the stakes at some game.
annotation.walkthrough: The outer letters of the three words make DRUDGE; handily DR is also the standard abbreviation for doctor, which may lead you astray.
annotation.definitionFit: A drudge is someone who does the dull, hard work.

entries.clue: Promising answer, not trusting to surrender lead (10)

indicatorNotes.surrender lead: the word gives up its first letter

blocks.note: SUSPICIOUS without its first letter S

annotation.surface: Someone refusing, out of distrust, to hand over the lead despite a promising reply.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lead' reads as a leash or the front position; in wordplay it is the first letter of the word.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both describe signs pointing to future success, as in a good omen.

entries.clue: Thus Russia’s banning odd parts for march music provider (5)

indicatorNotes.banning odd parts: the odd-numbered letters are removed, leaving the even ones

annotation.surface: Russia prohibiting parts of military band music.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s is 'is'. John Philip Sousa was the American composer of military marches such as The Stars and Stripes Forever.
annotation.definitionFit: Sousa wrote many famous marches.

entries.clue: Secretly take hold of oil producer (4)

blocks.note: the conjuror's verb for hiding a card in the hand
a tropical tree whose fruit is pressed for cooking oil

annotation.surface: Covertly seizing an oil company.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests corporate takeovers; the producer is a tree.
annotation.definitionFit: To palm something is to take it secretly in the hand; the palm tree produces oil.

entries.clue: Kind of wet, like a sap? (5)

blocks.note: a sap is a fool, a MUG; add -GY for 'like one'

annotation.surface: Describing someone feeble, a wet sap.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wet' and 'sap' both mean feeble person in British slang, which is the picture; the question mark admits MUGGY as 'like a mug' is invented.
annotation.definitionFit: Muggy weather is close and damp, a kind of wet.

entries.clue: Someone exploiting escort, skipping hotel (4)

indicatorNotes.skipping: to skip something is to miss it out, so USHER misses out its H

blocks.note: H = hotel in the phonetic alphabet, removed

annotation.surface: Someone taking advantage of a companion but not going to a hotel.
annotation.walkthrough: USHER minus H. Hotel is H in the radio alphabet.
annotation.definitionFit: A user is someone who exploits others.

entries.clue: Showman’s brief time recalled in papers (7)

indicatorNotes.brief: brief means short, so HOUR is cut short by its last letter
indicatorNotes.recalled: the letters are called back, read in reverse

annotation.surface: A performer's short spell recorded in the newspapers.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s stands for 'is'. 'Papers' are identity papers, ID, not newspapers.
annotation.definitionFit: Harry Houdini was the great escapologist and stage showman.

entries.clue: Try to ditch a chick (7)

blocks.note: to sling something is to ditch it

annotation.surface: Advice to dump a girlfriend.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chick' in the surface is slang for a young woman; the answer takes it literally as a baby bird.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a baby goose is one kind of chick, while the surface wants the slang sense of a young woman.

entries.clue: Site of growing fury in Circle Line (8)

indicatorNotes.in: the fury sits in, inside, the circle and line once they are joined

annotation.surface: Mounting rage among passengers on London's Circle Line.
annotation.walkthrough: OR(ANGER)Y: circle and line join as ORY first. 'Growing fury' pairs up as rising anger, but 'growing' belongs to the definition; the Circle Line is a London Underground route.
annotation.definitionFit: An orangery is a glasshouse where orange trees are grown.

entries.clue: Northern island holds onto otherwise Scottish council area (6)

indicatorNotes.holds: the island holds N inside it

blocks.note: a key is a low island, as in the Florida Keys

annotation.surface: A northern island clinging on to its separate identity.
annotation.walkthrough: OR + K(N)EY. The surface suggests Orkney itself, a northern island, which is fitting since the answer is one.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the archipelago off Scotland's north coast is governed as one of its 32 local authority areas.
